---
title: "Exercise · Engineering Through Stories"
---

A short, guided task. Complete it before moving on to the next lesson.

## Task

Listen to or read the Crossplane restaurant audio story (the reference example
under `reference-example/`). Then answer the following questions for each feature
you identify.

Pick any five features from the story — a line of dialogue, a sound effect, a
narration line, a character's voice, or a scene transition — and identify which
**stage of the architectural principle pipeline** produced it.

## Format

For each feature, write:

1. **Feature:** what you noticed (e.g. "the ticket printer sound when an order is
   placed").
2. **Pipeline stage:** which stage is responsible (Technical Model, Metaphor,
   Story/Scenes, Screenplay, or Audio Producer).
3. **Why:** a one-sentence justification.

::: {.callout-tip}
Use the mapping from the [lesson](index.qmd) to guide your identification. The
glossary also defines each stage.
:::

## Example

| Feature | Pipeline stage | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "One application environment, please." | Screenplay | This is dialogue written for the ear. |
| Customer = Developer | Metaphor | This is a mapping from the technical model to a familiar role. |
| The developer asks for a composite environment | Technical Model | This is a fact about how Crossplane works. |

## Success criteria

- [ ] You identified five features.
- [ ] Each feature is assigned to a pipeline stage.
- [ ] Each assignment has a one-sentence justification.

## Reflect

- Which stage was easiest to identify? Why?
- Which was hardest? What would help you tell them apart?
- Did anything in the story seem to belong to two stages at once?
